premises: Home braiding by family or friends is a feasible substitute for some customers.
customers.source: Unclear provisions: whether unpaid braiding for family and friends is covered. Assumed not covered (only braiding for pay is).

premises: What customers move to (home braiding by family and friends, unlicensed braiders) is of lower quality than the paid braiding it replaces.
customers.source: The curriculum covers cutting, coloring and chemical treatments; braiding is a small part or absent.

premises: Schools, licensed cosmetologists and braiders can organize and spend to change or defend the requirement at a cost below their stakes.
schools.source: 1,500 hours at a licensed cosmetology school (typical tuition $12,000 to $18,000)

premises: Some current braiders or new entrants choose to obtain the full license.
sellers.current.source: A full cosmetology license: 1,500 hours at a licensed cosmetology school ... and a state exam. Existing braiders have 12 months to comply.

premises: Braiders relocate to neighboring states on a meaningful scale.
sellers.current.source: Two neighboring states do not license braiding; their borders are a long drive from the main cities.

premises: Licensed cosmetologists take some of the customers who leave unlicensed braiders.
sellers.current.source: Bound: Anyone who braids for pay, and any business that employs them (licensed cosmetologists are the only legal braiders).

premises: Schools, licensed cosmetologists and braiders can organize and spend to change or defend the requirement at a cost below their stakes.
sellers.current.source: About 2,000 people braid for pay, mostly self-employed, many working from home or in small shops.
